body.x: AVING News selected ▲Ninebot’s “Segway Robot”, ▲Keekckers’ “Keecker”, ▲Somabar’s “Robotic Bartender”, ▲Cerevo’s “Tipron”, and ▲Sphero’s “BB-8” as the top five robotic products that were showcased at “CES 2016 (Consumer Technology Show)”, the world’s largest IT electronics and tech exhibition, which ran for four days from Wednesday the 6th to Saturday the 9th in Las Vegas.

Segway Robot is collaboratively created by Ninebot and Intel. It received much attention as Intel’s CEO rode it onto the stage for his keynote speech. It is like a normal electric scooter but it turns into a robot with a screen when users push a button. With Intel’s Atom processor and Intel® RealSense™ Technology, it can recognize and avoid obstacles. As it also supports a voice recognition function, it automatically follows users when they say, “Hi Segway, Follow me”.

The home robot "Keecker" is smaller yet smarter and brighter than the previous version. It has a beam projector that shows a 40-inch screen with HD 720p (1280x720) resolution and a 360-degree full 4.1 surround sound system. Also, its 360-degree camera protects users’ homes safely. Its operating system is Android 5, and its remote control supports both Android and iOS. Furthermore, it has various advanced sensors, including those for air quality and humidity, a compass, an accelerometer, and a gyroscope. It possesses a 2.7GHz Qualcomm 8084 Quad Core CPU and a 1TB hard drive with RAM of 3GB.

Receiving much attention with the “CES Best Innovative Award”, the smart cocktail maker “Robotic Bartender” is connected via Wi-Fi and enables users to make cocktails via their smartphones. When users select a certain cocktail, it automatically analyzes the ingredients and makes it with exact proportions. It can make more than 300 different kinds of beverages. It is also very sanitary, as it has an automatic cleaning system. It comes in white, black, orange, blue, and red.

“Tipron”, a transforming robot with a projector, is capable of projecting an 80-inch 720p HD resolution screen from 3 meters away. It can adjust its height and the angle of its neck. Users can change its projection location via a smartphone app. It also has keystone correction and auto focus functions to provide a pleasant video-watching experience. Furthermore, it is equipped with an IR sensor, giving it the ability to avoid obstacles. Its battery capacity is 5,800mAh, and it can be used for about two hours on a single charge. When it needs to recharge, it automatically returns to its charging station.

Sphero, an American startup, launched “BB-8”, a robot in the movie “Star Wars”, as a “connected toy”. This robot can be controlled by using a smartphone app or the “Force Band”, which is scheduled to be launched soon. It recognizes the movements of “Force Band”, and it moves along the direction of one’s arm and adjusts its speed according to the arm’s height.

“CES”, which is held every year in January by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is the world’s largest IT consumer electronics exhibition, showcasing global trends in the electronics and IT industry. AVING News, which has sent reporters to CES for 11 years, will introduce various up-to-date technologies and products showcased at CES 2016.
